answer: Latency-seeded work auction. Each agent identity must complete a random-delay puzzle whose solution seeds its bidding key; early bids are rejected, so a clone farm gains nothing by scale and each extra identity pays fresh compute plus a forfeited lotus deposit on abandon. Enforcement caps identities per payout address at the network's nadir performance percentile, forcing attackers to split rewards across costly keys. A basalt-signed audit log makes reuse detectable, so the marginal clone's expected payout falls below its registration and idle cost.
